This is a measurement of the new candidate, not a rescue of the old verdicts: the canonical verdicts of run 36092882496 and the diagnostic outcomes of batch diagnostic-failed-rerun-20260926 are preserved, never replaced, never reinterpreted and never merged. Two questions only: (a) does each failure reproduce on the freshly built latest main, and (b) how do the outcomes and the spec-241 measured per-call times compare with the source run and with the beta.36 measurement. Candidate delta, mechanically checked in the source repository: beta.36 -> beta.37 is 33 commits over 95 files, and none of them changes the benchmark path's executed behaviour. Eight changed files are inside the value-import closure of the headless entry (apps/cli/src/index.ts -> v3-run.ts:326 -> product-slices/thread-orchestration-root.ts:274), but none executes under the argv the benchmark actually uses (scripts/frontier-harness-harness.mjs:195 builds `best-agent run ...` with no --compact-dir): product-slices/compact.ts is enabled only by --compact-dir (v3-run.ts:1402, v3-run-options.ts:457/956), so compactedContextSelected stays false and v3-prompt-composition.ts:305 appends nothing; native-runtime-bridge.ts is reached only through applicationRootFamily.nativeBridge (TUI / subagent loop) while run goes through runV3SinglePromptWithThreadOrchestration; dimsdk/shared/git-branch.ts has no call site in v3-run.ts; the remaining changed files are TUI-only slices and pages, generated product manifests, tests and docs. So, exactly as with beta.34 -> beta.36, no changed file lands on the benchmark path's executed behaviour, and any outcome difference in this batch is run-to-run variance rather than an effect of the new code; the batch cannot support a capability claim.
